batch_strategy: Resolve structure-dependent solvent-response transitions and endpoint-specific failures using matched condition pairs, selected loading contrasts, and transfer tests in common carbonyl families. Prioritize questions left open by measured feedback, including opposite historical error directions within a family. Use the supplied predictions as model behavior rather than measured evidence; quantile widths do not define an acquisition ranking.

choices.reason: Nitrobenzophenone at 20/1 and 150 uL, predicted 8.55/22.17 mL, starts a matched pair at a third amount. The 100 uL series rises through 10/1 but has low completion at 50/1, whereas the 50 uL series rises sharply from 20/1 to 50/1 (4862e2fb71344ce16021; 5b706e17e8412d02342f). This tests whether either pattern transfers.

Complete the nitrobenzophenone 20/1-to-50/1 pair at 150 uL, predicted 20.69/49.15 mL. Comparing this curve with aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and 5b706e17e8412d02342f, and the contrasting 100 uL series, can distinguish amount-associated structure from an isolated conflicting endpoint. It cannot establish repeatability by itself.

Para-aminobenzonitrile at 5/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 40.07/99.47 mL. It completes a fixed-amount response from b21061720e23b7a5bdcb at 2/1 and supplies an amount contrast to b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 at 5/1. Together with the selected meta-isomer conditions, it separates positional response from loading differences.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile at 2/1 and 50 uL, predicted 10.41/24.27 mL, matches the para-isomer loading in b21061720e23b7a5bdcb and contrasts with the measured meta 100 uL condition 53a1acff30433cff819f. This makes the selected two-isomer response comparison interpretable without assuming amount invariance.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile at 5/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 34.45/85.97 mL. Paired with its selected 2/1 condition and the selected para 5/1 condition, it tests whether the positional onset difference measured at 100 uL in 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 persists at fixed lower loading.

Ethyl aminocrotonate at 5/1 and 50 uL with 200 uL DCM is predicted at 5.80/14.01 mL. Matched observations 7383949c431e18f39597 and 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 establish a much steeper 10/1-to-20/1 rise than previously predicted. This anchors the earlier part of that response and tests the proposed low 5/1 completion.

Ethyl nicotinate at 5/1 and 150 uL, predicted 29.91/71.01 mL, bridges identical-loading observations 22f82413c75481d74e9b at 2/1 and c76d0420b34df595c0c9 at 10/1. It identifies a basic heteroaromatic transition and tests transfer from the larger pyridyl-ketone response in 49201b5817f204116f7f.

Methyl anthranilate at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 20.49/42.44 mL, beyond its modest 5/1 result 645cb06b9e2a33b6044b. Comparison with ethyl anthranilate at 20/1 in 74541dbf8571f881c454 tests ester-side structural transfer. Their loading solvents and solvent volumes differ, so any difference cannot be assigned solely to methyl versus ethyl.

Methyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 17.85/38.43 mL. Its 5/1 and 20/1 observations cd566862a517dd7cdc8d and f402144b8672dd5ab2ab bracket a response whose weak endpoint was historically underestimated. This tests intermediate transfer, while retaining the 100-versus-50 uL loading difference.

The cyclopropyl beta-ketoester at 5/1 and 50 uL, predicted 12.21/24.48 mL, starts a matched pair with its selected 10/1 condition. Measurements e3a799d0fa90b649a157 and 668279c54bbf75e86496 exposed opposite historical error directions at 20/1 and 10/1. The pair tests where its steep response develops.

Complete the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester 5/1-to-10/1 pair at 50 uL, predicted 23.32/48.88 mL. This identifies a local slope at fixed loading and provides a same-ratio amount comparison with 668279c54bbf75e86496 at 100 uL. Both are useful before transferring its large 20/1 response to other beta-ketoesters.

The methacrylate/acetoacetate diester at 10/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 44.65/110.75 mL. The same ratio at 150 uL measured 36.92/94.21 mL in ca467c94f14b2219503e. This amount contrast tests whether the response scale transfers across loading and whether the current large prediction overshoots at the lower amount.

Methyl benzoylformate at 20/1 and 50 uL, predicted 13.08/35.78 mL, connects the 50/1 observation 7caf1db075b91197ba34 at the same amount with the 20/1 observation e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 at 150 uL. It tests alpha-ketoester response shape and amount association against the beta-ketoester comparisons.

Diethyl malonate at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at 17.45/37.78 mL, a large rise beyond its matched 10/1 measurement of 5.12/6.85 mL in 08ae0e5f727afabf1e71. This directly tests an unmeasured late transition for two ester groups and guards against transferring beta-ketoester response scales through acceptor count alone.

Diethyl phenylmalonate at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at 14.19/26.83 mL. With the selected diethyl malonate condition, it tests alpha-phenyl substitution at the same ratio, sample volume and PE loading-solvent volume. Existing anchors f82f2844c7e27afd32bb and fa1a4a2aa332b091b615 use other amounts; densities also differ between compounds.

Para-methoxyacetophenone at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at 19.87/41.64 mL. Observations f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0 and 5f2fc9606fb31b009ccc at 100 uL showed almost unchanged completion between 2/1 and 10/1. This tests whether a later transition actually occurs, retaining the amount difference.

Ortho-methoxyacetophenone at 50/1 and 150 uL, predicted 20.70/47.54 mL, extends matched observations 50fbcf5ece9bd5fc2d70 and ebdeaba52880c7eade16. Their onset remained near 5 mL while completion increased. This tests the proposed delayed onset rise and whether the two endpoints require different solvent-response slopes.

Naphthaldehyde at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 20.82/35.41 mL. Existing 20/1 records 783cf2454912fc14bb80 at 100 uL and a917c928912c74862968 at 150 uL have very different onsets; the latter also has V2 slightly below V1. The new amount and the 50 uL weak-eluent anchor 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49 help assess this inconsistent region.

Biphenyl-substituted butyrophenone at 10/1 with unchanged loading is predicted at 6.15/20.15 mL. Completion decreased from 25.62 mL at 5/1 in c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8 to 17.50 mL at 20/1 in cb534927304d5c892100. The intermediate tests whether that decrease extends across the region or the 5/1 interval is locally unusual.

5-Chloropentan-2-one at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 8.77/15.53 mL, starts a fixed-loading pair. Its measured coverage is only pure EA in a63ce210564bfb05f06c. This tests transfer from the catalog's abundant aromatic ketones to an exposed aliphatic carbonyl with a remote chloride.

Complete the 5-chloropentan-2-one pair at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 18.28/34.15 mL. Two labels beyond a63ce210564bfb05f06c identify a response scale rather than an isolated endpoint. They test whether the predicted substantial onset increase generalizes from aromatic to aliphatic ketones.

1-Phenylethanol at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 17.54/25.54 mL. The measured decrease from 2/1 in f559a4634c60d81f5f15 to 5/1 in 994a1f65509549a84ede confirmed the earlier proposed dip. This tests the predicted rebound at identical loading and prevents an unsupported monotonic alcohol correction.

4-Phenylbutan-2-ol at 10/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 41.11/68.94 mL. Matched measurements c9ad01493d938f825117 and 985361f6699d97f9464f established steep onset growth but relatively compact intervals at 2/1 and 5/1. This tests whether completion subsequently broadens as strongly as predicted.

The remote tertiary alcohol at 10/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 38.51/63.43 mL. Its matched 5/1 anchor bf09d868ed4d68a97b40 measured 18.92/28.63 mL. Comparison with the selected remote secondary alcohol uses the same ratio and PE loading conditions, testing steric-environment transfer separately for onset and completion.

2-Isopropylphenol at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 11.32/19.60 mL. Identical-loading observations 0120f093f01a659610ef in pure EA and 68a01853008546de06a1 at 50/1 bracket a substantial response. This locates an intermediate for a sterically encumbered phenolic donor and tests transfer from the alcohol curves.

Trifluoromethoxyphenol at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 7.10/11.38 mL and starts a matched pair with 20/1. Its only measured anchor, 2a7062ac85d66260b3be, is pure EA at 150 uL. The pair tests the modest predicted response of a phenolic donor plus ether without assuming donor count determines retention.

Complete the trifluoromethoxyphenol pair at 20/1 and 100 uL, predicted 11.50/19.06 mL. Fixed loading separates its solvent-response slope from the amount difference to 2a7062ac85d66260b3be. Comparing this curve with 2-isopropylphenol tests phenolic structural transfer, with their different loading solvents kept explicit.

Unmeasured meta-fluoropropiophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 6.77/17.03 mL, with observed similarity 0.633. It starts a matched response pair, using meta-bromopropiophenone observation 4c10cf623fbb8793829f and para-fluoroacetophenone observation 059b09a46d0835771fd6 as structural references rather than equivalent conditions.

Complete the new meta-fluoropropiophenone pair at 50/1 with unchanged loading, predicted 9.14/22.73 mL. This tests the proposed modest weak-eluent slope after changing halogen position and acyl-chain length relative to measured aromatic ketones. Two labels provide a scaffold-specific response test rather than novelty alone.

Unmeasured 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 7.94/19.11 mL, with observed similarity 0.52. It starts a fixed-loading pair. Ortho-methylbenzaldehyde measurement d626f5ddb709bc11257a and mesityl methyl ketone measurement 4b104d6f7556c8bc3a51 motivate a test of proximal methyl substitution around aromatic carbonyls.

Complete the 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde pair at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 9.33/22.21 mL. The modest proposed change from 20/1 tests whether methyl-substituted aldehydes preserve small endpoint slopes despite larger responses elsewhere in the carbonyl catalog. This supplies useful low-to-moderate retention coverage.

Cinnamic acid at 10/1 with 100 uL sample and 1500 uL DCM is predicted at 34.25/84.05 mL. Matched observations 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286 and 1e971da91b3a8229f0e0 showed onset increasing only from 8.32 to 11.88 mL between 2/1 and 5/1. This tests the proposed later onset acceleration after the large loading-solvent-volume interaction was weakened.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen families require distinct solvent-response transition locations. At matched loading, meta-aminobenzonitrile rises strongly between 2/1 and 5/1, whereas ethyl aminocrotonate has a large rise between 10/1 and 20/1. Positional transfer, amount transfer and interpolation to nicotinates or amino esters remain incompletely constrained.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels that identify transition location can prevent a correction learned for one nitrogen environment from shifting entire response curves for other nitrogen families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which positional and family-specific response differences persist when loading is matched, and do the unmeasured intermediate conditions follow the current transition scales?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzophenone's 100 uL measurements show ordinary completion growth through 10/1 followed by a low 50/1 endpoint, while its 50 uL completion rises sharply from 20/1 to 50/1. An amount-dependent weak-eluent response and variability among records remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This region has generated large historical errors in opposite directions. A third matched curve can constrain the relationship without teaching a universal reversed solvent response or asserting a causal amount effect.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, does the 20/1-to-50/1 response resemble the 100 uL decline, the 50 uL rise, or neither?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl environment affects onset, completion and transition location separately. The 1-phenylethanol decrease from 2/1 to 5/1 is measured, while the remote secondary alcohol rises steeply and the constrained tertiary benzylic alcohol retains relatively compact measured intervals. Transfer to remote tertiary alcohols and substituted phenols remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These comparisons can reduce inappropriate sharing of endpoint slopes across donor-containing compounds and distinguish an onset shift from expansion of the elution interval.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 10/1, do the remote secondary and tertiary alcohols develop the predicted completion expansion, and does 1-phenylethanol rebound after its measured 5/1 dip?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl topology and additional oxygen placement require different response curves. Methyl acetoacetate's 20/1 completion was underestimated, the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester's 10/1 response was overestimated after its 20/1 failure, and the multi-oxygen diester's 10/1 completion was underestimated. Alpha-ketoester and malonate transitions provide useful contrasting tests.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Carbonyl compounds occupy much of the candidate distribution. Local curves and topology comparisons can correct transition placement without imposing a common scale based on oxygen or acceptor count.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does the matched cyclopropyl 5/1-to-10/1 curve rise, and does diethyl malonate develop the predicted large transition beyond its measured 10/1 condition?

hypotheses.content: Cinnamic acid has closely similar measured 2/1-to-5/1 completion responses under the recorded 1500 and 2000 uL DCM loading-solvent volumes. This weakens a large volume interaction in that range. Its broad elution intervals and the proposed onset acceleration beyond 5/1 remain useful response-shape questions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The completed volume comparison redirects acquisition toward solvent-response shape and can prevent the model from attributing a large retention change to a loading-solvent feature unsupported by these observations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 10/1 and fixed 1500 uL loading-solvent volume, does onset accelerate toward the predicted 34.25 mL, or does most additional volume remain associated with completion?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl substitutions can move onset and completion transitions differently. Para-methoxyacetophenone has nearly unchanged measured completion between 2/1 and 10/1, while ortho-methoxyacetophenone retains a low onset through 20/1 despite increasing completion. Whether either develops the currently predicted later onset rise remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific labels can improve transfer across common aromatic ketones and aldehydes, including modest-retention substitutions, without propagating large responses from multi-acceptor aromatic compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the methoxyacetophenones show the proposed late transitions, and can the model correctly transfer more modest response slopes to the unmeasured fluoropropiophenone and dimethylbenzaldehyde?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes sharpened transition-location questions rather than supporting a global retention correction. Aminobenzonitrile completion at 2/1 was historically overpredicted by about 7–8 mL, following substantial underestimates at 5/1. Ethyl aminocrotonate's 10/1 completion was overpredicted by 55.37 mL, while its measured 20/1 value remains large; its increase therefore develops much later than previously assumed. The cyclopropyl beta-ketoester likewise showed an intermediate overestimate after a weak-endpoint underestimate, whereas methyl acetoacetate and the multi-oxygen diester still exposed underestimation. These results motivate local response measurements and selected amount contrasts. The 1-phenylethanol dip was confirmed, unlike the earlier rejected naphthylethanol onset dip; the remote secondary alcohol pair also showed less completion at 2/1 and a more compact 5/1 interval than generic alcohol transfer suggested. Para-methoxyacetophenone's modest 10/1 result motivates testing a later transition. The biphenyl-ketone pair introduced a measured completion decrease that deserves an intermediate check without assuming reproducibility. Nitrobenzophenone's new 100 uL anchors form a coherent early rise but do not resolve its conflicting weak-eluent records. The P/O 5/1 result lies near the stronger-eluent measurements and places its large observed change between 5/1 and 10/1; its available ratio coverage is now sufficient to defer further amount variants. Benzyl benzoate's 50/1 label confirms substantial growth before 100/1, with onset and completion changing differently thereafter. Cinnamic acid's two loading-solvent-volume series agree closely enough to weaken a large volume interaction, so its next measurement addresses the unmeasured 10/1 response. All errors discussed here are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 labels address several reusable relationships across the Row-distribution. Matched aminobenzonitrile comparisons, the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester pair, the aliphatic chloroketone pair and the phenol pair identify local solvent-response slopes. Nitrogen and carbonyl intermediates target transition locations exposed by opposite historical error directions. Nitrobenzophenone's third-amount curve and naphthaldehyde's additional 20/1 amount probe inconsistent regions while keeping amount associations distinct from causation or record variability. The alcohol comparisons test whether onset and completion should share a correction, and the acid experiment extends a response after its loading-solvent comparison became less compelling. Two new aromatic-carbonyl pairs test structural transfer at modest predicted retention, complementing failure repair without selecting novelty for its own sake. Numerous interchangeable amount variants and neutral halide/ether analogs offer less additional discrimination given existing coverage and recent accurate low-retention feedback. Between-compound loading differences remain explicit. V2 minus V1 is treated as elution-interval width, and the single predictor's quantile widths are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. All 32 IDs retain the exact supplied premeasurement predictions associated with this packet hash; numerical predictions in reasons are rounded descriptions only. The entire batch is fixed before any new label reveal.
